documented_prior: a[jid] ~ dnorm(0,0.5); w[wid] ~ dnorm(0,0.5); sigma ~ dexp(1)
notes: Scores of 20 wines (a white and a red flight of 10, French and from New Jersey) by 9 judges (French and American), blind to the wines (Wines2012.Rd). McElreath's 2020 course, week 5 (homework/week05/week05_script.R), fits m1: the standardized score ~ normal(a[judge] + w[wine], sigma), a and w each normal(0, 0.5) without a hyperprior; its m2a, m2b and m3 regress the score on wine.amer, judge.amer and flight without the judge and wine indices. The fixed scales keep the grouping and are named in the formula (rugby, #15). wine.amer, judge.amer and flight are unused usable columns. Outside check: m1 replaces the reading's combination of the two models.

formula: h ~ male + (1 | pair) + (1 | pair:ifelse(M == 1, pair, member))
notes: Hay fever in 3,807 twin pairs (Hopper et al. 1990), stored as 20 pair patterns of two members, each with a pair-level frequency weight freq. The publisher's solution to MLMUS4 exercise 16.11 (ex16_11_twinhay.do) fits the ADE model meprobit h male || pair:, fweight(freq) || k:, with k = pair for monozygotic (M == 1) and member for dizygotic pairs, and derives the additive and dominance variances; Rabe-Hesketh's 2010 German Stata Users talk (pp. 19-21) fits it by gllamm, then the AE model constraining the two variances equal. The k level is a unit no column holds, so it stays in the formula only. Outside check: the solution's model replaces the inferred one.
